page: Microsoft Azure E8_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for workloads requiring a high memory-to-vCPU allocation. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs backed by 4 physical cores and 8 threads from an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualization is managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with 35 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets, including AVX-512 with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), BMI2, and AES-NI hardware cryptography. The instance contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

The instance provides 64.0 GB of memory, establishing a generous 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio typical of memory-intensive infrastructure. It does not bundle any local storage, meaning all disk operations rely on attached remote storage solutions. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the instance. Memory throughput testing reflects balanced performance, registering 414.9 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, 49.73 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 34.64 GB/sec for large-block writes.

In synthetic and real-world benchmark evaluations, the E8_v4 demonstrates mid-tier CPU and workload execution. Geekbench testing shows a single-core score of 1237.0 and a multi-core score of 4762.0, while PassMark reports an overall CPU score of 8479.44. In memory-dependent application tests, the instance processed 6.96 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved 6.65 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound LLM prompt processing is limited, scoring 11.96 tokens per second on a 7B model. Given the absence of local disks and strong memory density, the E8_v4 is best aligned with in-memory databases, Redis caches, mid-sized relational database servers utilizing remote block storage, and general enterprise memory-heavy services.
description: Microsoft Azure E8_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered around an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores clocked at 2.6 GHz with 35 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, with support for AVX-512 and hardware encryption. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark results show balanced throughput, including 6.96 million Redis SET operations per second, 6.65 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and a PassMark CPU score of 8479.44. Due to its large memory allocation alongside moderate compute and lack of local NVMe disks, the E8_v4 fits in-memory caching layers, relational database hosting, and memory-intensive enterprise business systems.
